onnx.static_shapes: yes once batch_size is fixed to 1: input and output are always 1 x 4 x 3072 x 256
onnx.notes: Only Conv, ConvTranspose, BatchNormalization, Relu, MatMul, Add, Mul and Transpose; no shape ops, no complex or FFT ops. Batch is the only dynamic dimension; to get a fully static graph for QNN, fix it with onnxruntime's make_dynamic_shape_fixed (--dim_param batch_size --dim_value 1) or the session option for free dimension overrides.

audio_in.layout: planar (2, n): channel 0 = left, channel 1 = right; mono files: copy the channel
audio_in.scale: decoded PCM in [-1, 1]; no normalisation or peak scaling (see notes.normalisation)

stft.window: periodic Hann: w[k] = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2 * pi * k / 7680), k = 0..7679 (torch.hann_window(n_fft, periodic=True))
stft.pad: reflect 3840 samples at both ends of the chunk (numpy 'reflect', the edge sample is not repeated: x[-1] = x[1])
stft.transform: X[t, f] = sum_k xpad[t*1024 + k] * w[k] * exp(-2 pi i f k / 7680), f = 0..3840 (onesided rfft, not normalised)

model_input.index: input[0, c, f, t] for f in 0..dim_f-1 (frequency), t in 0..255 (frame)
model_input.zero_bins: set bins f = 0, 1, 2 to 0 in all 4 channels before running the model

model_output.meaning: the vocals' spectrogram, same channel layout as the input
model_output.to_complex: left = out[0,0] + i*out[0,1], right = out[0,2] + i*out[0,3]; bins 3072..3840 are 0

istft.match: torch.istft(n_fft, hop, periodic Hann, center=True, length=None)
steps: overlap-add frame_t at offset t * 1024 into a buffer of 268800 samples
overlap-add w[k]^2 the same way into an envelope buffer
divide the buffer by the envelope, then drop 3840 samples at both ends
pad = gen + trim - (n mod gen)   (gen = 253440, trim = 3840)
padded = [trim zeros | mix | pad zeros], length L = trim + n + pad
for start = 0, step, 2*step, ... while start < L (step = 195840):
end = min(start + chunk, L); part = padded[start:end] zero-filled to chunk samples
M = end - start; h[k] = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2 * pi * k / (M - 1)), k = 0..M-1 (numpy.hanning(M), symmetric)
vocals = out[trim : trim + n] / div[trim : trim + n]   (div is 0 only at padded[0], which is dropped)

trim_alternative.source: KUIELab mdx-net-submission demix_base (the original): about 23% fewer model runs, no window
steps: pad = gen - (n mod gen); padded = [trim zeros | mix | pad zeros | trim zeros]
for start = 0, gen, 2*gen, ... while start < n + pad: y = iSTFT(model(STFT(padded[start:start+chunk])))
keep y[trim : chunk - trim] (gen samples) and append
trim_alternative.laptop_quality: not run; ov25 is the measured mode

postprocess_for_lyrify.mono: vocals_mono = (left + right) / 2; mix_mono = (left + right) / 2 of the input
postprocess_for_lyrify.gate_frames: 1 s frames at 44.1 kHz (44,100 samples, last partial frame dropped): rms_v, rms_m; a frame is vocal when rms_m > 1e-3 and rms_v > 0.2 * rms_m (the V2 rule, unchanged)
postprocess_for_lyrify.whisper_input: vocals_mono resampled 44.1 -> 16 kHz (the bench uses julius.resample_frac, a windowed sinc), then the vocal chunks of phone_wcpp_variants.vocal_chunks
postprocess_for_lyrify.secondary_stem: not needed; if wanted, instrumental = mix - vocals * 1.021 (compensate)

notes.normalisation: python-audio-separator scales the mix to a 0.9 peak before separating and multiplies the result by the original peak; that only changes the stem's gain, so the bench and this spec feed the mix as decoded and take the stem as the model gives it.
notes.denoise: off (audio-separator's enable_denoise default); it would run the model twice per chunk
notes.reference_implementation: lyrify-bench/scripts/sep_mdx.py: hann_periodic, stft, istft, run_chunk, demix (numpy; stft/istft match torch.stft/istft to float32 precision, `sep_mdx.py selftest`)
